items.title: GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect
items.summary:
If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.

It starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon. A greenscreened science communicator then appears, rubs their forehead, and shows us a video of a ship disappearing over the horizon. Checkmate. 

It's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos. Now you're enrolled in a never ending lesson plan which features such insights as 'an all-meat diet is not good for you,' 'the moon landing was real,' and 'hating women is not in fact based .'

The total effect of this is that the most ignorant and dishonest quacks and provocateurs get to set the level of discourse, and instead of investigating new metaphorical horizons in topics that interest you, you wind up watching people debate the existence of the actual horizon.

Which brings me to Grand Theft Auto 6. Despite making $3.79 billion on its launch day, it's easy to stumble across confident social media claims that it's a total flop and everyone's going to refund it. According to popular X posts, GTA 6 doesn't even let you steal cars anymore, and there are hundreds of Metacritic user reviewers insisting that it's far-left propaganda rather than the mass-market entertainment product it obviously is.

It's the videogame discourse version of flat eartherism. The millions of people playing GTA 6 do…
items.t: GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect

items.title: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
items.summary:
Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.

As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval. Stoic, nonchalant, calm, composed, resigned; whatever you want to call one of GTA 6's new protagonists, Rockstar says it carefully crafted his already iconic demeanor by pulling from a Steve McQueen classic and real-life veterans.

The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid . Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway.

"Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."

He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers ) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks.

"These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."…

items.title: GTA 6's massive casino and sick go-kart track are currently closed, but I'm hoping we can trust those 'coming soon' signs 🙏
items.summary:
I'd just stolen my very first airplane in GTA 6 and was happily cruising over the city when I looked out my window and saw an enormous purple building. I banked, slowed down, and flew a bit closer to read the huge sign on the roof.

VICE CITY CASINO 

Oh, hell yes. I was so excited to throw my carefully accumulated three hundred dollars away on poker and slots that I immediately attempted my very first landing. After the explosion and my miraculous resurrection, I rushed back to the casino and crashed again, this time with my body into the locked front doors.

The casino in GTA 6 is closed. Trust me, I tried every door, and the only one that opened was a utility closet. 

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) I was early into my playthrough, still in Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 story missions , so I thought maybe there'll be some mission that unlocks the casino so I can play some poker, try my luck at the slots, and maybe bet on the also-closed dog track—I assume it's a dog track because I've seen dogs in GTA 6, but no horses—that's right next door to the casino.

Nope! I'm now 100% done with the main story and that casino is still closed. And that's not the only business in GTA 6 that isn't open for business. Not even a half-mile away from the casino there's a go-cart track called Hot Skidz sporting a huge "Coming Soon" sign. I saw that early in my game as well, and checked back later. Still closed. I also found a second, smaller casino. Also closed.

items.title: Forget the Lighthouse, GTA 6’s Best Minigame Is a Full-Blown Zombie Shooter That Will Take You Hours To Beat
items.summary:
To say I was up until midnight last night with GTA 6 is technically correct, but not the full picture. What I was actually doing was headshotting undead nightmares in Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, a moreish isometric twin-stick shooter that lives inside Jason's PS5-alike JoySystem.

You play it briefly with Cal during the story, and it impressed me enough to want to beat it fully. After nearly four hours, I still haven't. 

It's clearly inspired by the Sony-published Dead Nation from 2010, but it mashes the zombie slaying with a roguelike deckbuilder. Every time an enemy squelches, their blood splattering the pavement, you gain XP, and at each new level you pick a card to adjust your build. Basic cards boost movement speed, fire rate, damage or critical hit chance, but rarer cards transform your tactics, such as one that doubles your damage given and received. 

Your goal is to collect six gears strewn around a deceptively large map and leave via a rooftop chopper. You'll die a lot, but on each run you'll learn a little more about the world's layout and discover new cards to experiment with.

The satisfaction of Street Trash 3 is in crafting a build on the fly from the cards you're dealt, and in feeling your power spiral. You're constantly levelling up and that escalation, the way your build rapidly grows and branches depending on what you find, reminds me a lot of Vampire Survivors . Like that game, it's most fun when you lean into a specific skill: the closest I've come to victory was when I swapped my pistol for a micro-SMG, buffing and buffing my fire rate until the…

(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Playing on school computers has been a rite of passage for many young PC gamers, whether through dedicated edutainment titles or rogue installations by chancing pupils. But fantasy novelist Scott Lynch went one step further: he took the school computers home.

"My mother worked for our school district, so I'd occasionally have the chance to sneak into the computer lab, or we would borrow and Apple II over the summer," Lynch says. "When we did that, I borrowed Infocom games … text-only adventure games from the '80s like Zork, Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Planetfall, A Mind Forever voyaging. I was really into those when I was about 12."

Text-based adventures would eventually become a defining feature of Lynch's life, albeit in a different format. His debut novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora , was published in 2006, charting the schemes and adventures of a group of master con artists called The Gentleman Bastards. Two further novels in The Gentleman Bastard Sequence have since followed: 2007's Red Seas Under Red Skies , and 2013's The Republic of Thieves

David O'Reilly, an environment artist who worked at Rockstar for 12 years on games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Grand Theft Auto 5, and the just-released GTA 6, recently started a YouTube channel called Game World Art where he explores videogame environments. For the last year and a half or so, he's chatted about those games and others from his point of view, sharing tidbits about the tech involved in making them—and now that GTA 6 is out, he's showing off his work and offering some impressions.

"To set expectations, this is not a Rockstar insider-type channel, it's not telling you exactly how Rockstar makes their worlds, this is more about seeing these kinds of open world games—and this one in particular—through my eyes and my perspective as an environment artist," he said in the video. 

In his impressions video, he cruises around for a while and talks about his changing relationship to Rockstar games. Given that putting them together was literally his day job, he couldn't enjoy games like RDR 2 and GTA 5 "to anywhere near the extent" that can enjoy GTA 6—since he left the studio in 2023, he's got some distance from the final game. That doesn't mean he's turning the analytical part of his brain off entirely, though, as he stopped here and there to critique the world he saw.

items.title: American Psycho Remake From Director Luca Guadagnino No Longer Happening
items.summary:
Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.

The Challengers and Call Me by Your Name movie maker delivered the disappointing news when asked for an update on Deadline's Crew Call podcast. He admitted the script for the project that he read, which was penned by the writer behind The Bourne Ultimatum and Side Effects, was "fantastic" but not something he can continue working on.

"American Psycho, which is a fantastic script from Scott Z. Burns, unfortunately, is not happening for me, as we speak," Guadagnino said.

Guadagnino has more than proven himself as a name capable of handling the weight of a property on the level of American Psycho, which is exactly why movie fans were so excited to hear he could be attached to the project in 2024. Although fans have referred to what would have become his slice into the well-established movie universe as a 'remake,' at the time of its announcement, Lionsgate teased that the project would have been more of an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho novel, rather than a remake of Christian Bale's 2000 movie .

Updates on Guadagnino's American Psycho have been few and far between in the years since its announcement, though. Elvis star Austin Butler was once in the running for the role of Patrick Bateman, as was Euphoria's Jacob Elordi. It was reported in October 2025 that the film would not gender-swap its lead role .

I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical. 

You do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo , although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well. 

(Image credit: Silver Lining Interactive) This isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best. 

But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left.

There are four Mambas to scan with the WAiNK It app in the counties around Port Gellhorn, so this one is a little more involved than the previous cars. 

In a farmhouse garage north of Leonida State Prison The first Mamba GT is in the garage of a farmhouse to the north of Leonida State Prison, which is southeast of Gellhorn. Head north up the main road to the east of the prison until you spot a private property gate on the left side of the road, opposite a building on the other side with Gruppe6 written on it. 

Smash the gate and head up the track to the house where you'll find the wreck in the garage to the left of it (you can enter via the backdoor). There's also a little cash in a box here, too.

In a garage near Ambrosia gas station The second wrecked car is in the town of Ambrosia, east of Port Gellhorn, near the Xero Gas - Ambrosia station and the purchasable Wyatt Motors garage. Head right down the side of the gas station, turn right into the alley, and continue a little way until you spot a white garage door to your right, next to a big blue garage door. But even in this petrolheaded company, GTA 6 stands out.

E.T. has been cited as a contributing factor in the US video game industry crash of 1983—one of many poor-quality 8-bit titles that hollowed out the gaming market in the States. items.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'

One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). In a chat with The Examined Game , Skyrim lead Bruce Nesmith reflected on the reaction some Fallout old-heads had to Bethesda's acquisition of the series.

"There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout licence to do Fallout 3. For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011. I suspect Nesmith is muddling the initial negative reaction with, well, the more modern one, which is shaped in large part by Obsidian's excellent Fallout: New Vegas from 2010.

"We had to prove them wrong", recalls Nesmith, "and fortunately we did, because Fallout 3 was embraced even by a lot of our sceptics". "Save me."

Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead.

But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow.

I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped.

items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.summary:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.
items.t: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
items.t: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
